html:
SMTO-PSM-0008 — Parameter Store is unavailable

GUID: 004b5429-99cc-4763-84d8-47b352afb53b
Slug: parameter-unavailable
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't read one of the saved parameters your request mentions, so it paused the task before starting it. Nothing has run, and your saved parameters were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the message SMTO shows under your request. It names the parameter and may say the storage is busy, out of space, read-only, corrupt, or had an input/output error. The cause decides the fix; for example a busy store just needs a moment, while a full disk needs space freed.
  2. If it says storage is busy, wait a minute and select Check again. Another save was still in progress, and a second look usually succeeds once it finishes.
  3. If it says the parameter's saved record is invalid, select Open Parameter Store, open that parameter, re-enter its value and context, select Save, then select Check again. SMTO can't use a parameter whose saved details are broken, and saving a corrected version replaces them.
  4. If it says the storage is out of space, read-only, corrupt or had an input/output error, send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Those problems are on the server computer itself, and only someone with access to it can fix them.

What success looks like

  • After Check again, the message under your request says the references were resolved, and the task starts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Ask them not to delete the Parameter Store data to clear the error; it holds your saved parameters.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • While accepting the task, the Parameter Store lookup (get_exact), a saved binding read, or record_use raised an exception, so references could not be captured and the task is held.

What this means

  • Exact parameter lookup or record_use raises an exception while creating the accepted reference snapshot. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Exact parameter lookup or record_use raises an exception while creating the accepted reference snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect which storage action failed; this generic catch does not prove a filesystem permission problem.

How to fix it

  • Open the Runtime message's details: the diagnostic reason (lookup_failed, invalid_record, invalid_snapshot or usage_failed) and storage cause (busy, permission, full, corrupt, io) come from src/agent_runtime/parameters/diagnostics.py. Fix that condition for the Parameter Store database at agent_parameters_db_path (free disk space, restore write permission, wait for a competing writer, or restore a corrupt database from backup), then choose Check again. Do not delete the database or bypass checks to make the store look healthy.
  • Restore the supported Parameter Store service according to the retained diagnostic, preserve entries, and retry admission only after access works.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual store service fault is resolved and admission can read and record use of the intended entries.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
